items.title: VI Live: AZ-invaller Oufkir deelt genadeklap uit aan Utrecht
items.summary: Zaterdag staan er vier Eredivisie-wedstrijden gepland. NEC gaat op bezoek bij promovendus Willem II, FC Utrecht ontvangt AZ en Fortuna Sittard staat tegenover SC Cambuur. Het duel van PSV volgen we in een aparte live, de rest komt in deze VI Live uitvoerig aan bod.

items.title: Eberl geeft geruststellende update na schrikmoment rondom Musiala
items.summary: Jamal Musiala maakt het goed, zo heeft technisch directeur van Bayern München Max Eberl laten weten. De 23-jarige Duitser werd onwel tijdens het oefenduel tussen Bayern en RB Leipzig. Eberl gaf na afloop een korte update.

items.title: VI Live: Excelsior ondanks vroege tegengoal geen niemendalletje voor PSV
items.summary: PSV hoopt zich zaterdag te revancheren voor de valse Eredivisie-start van vorige week. Na de remise tegen Fortuna Sittard neemt de kampioen van Nederland het zaterdag om 20.00 uur op tegen Excelsior, de koploper na de eerste speelronde. Mis niets van deze wedstrijd in de VI Live.

items.title: Transfer roundup: Aston Villa close on Japan keeper Zion Suzuki as Emiliano Martínez nears exit
items.summary: PSG sign Spain’s Ferran Torres from Barcelona Djed Spence completes move to Inter from Spurs Aston Villa are preparing for the potential exit of goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez by accelerating a move for Parma’s Zion Suzuki. Juventus have revived their interest in Martínez, who is open to leaving after six seasons at Villa and is increasingly likely to depart during this transfer window. Villa are advancing a deal to sign Suzuki as the Argentina No 1’s replacement. Villa dismissed an offer from Juve for Martínez earlier this summer, but Juve have now revisited a move for the 33-year-old, who is under contract until 2029. Juve are also thought to be monitoring Ederson, now of Fenerbahce, and Tottenham’s Guglielmo Vicario. Suzuki was poised to join Paris Saint-Germain this week, but the Champions League winners, who defeated Villa in the Super Cup in Salzburg on Wednesday, pulled out of a deal worth about €35m (£30m). items.title: Inter heeft beet: Spence treedt in de voetsporen van Dumfries

items.title: Tahaui scoort bij debuut voor NEC: 'Droom komt uit'
items.summary: Voor Adam Tahaui werd de wedstrijd tussen Willem II en NEC er een om niet snel te vergeten. De 21-jarige middenvelder debuteerde niet alleen voor de Nijmeegse club, maar opende ook nog de score in Tilburg. Na afloop was Tahaui dolblij.

items.title: Championship roundup: Middlesbrough seal comeback win; West Brom beat Norwich
items.summary: Lankshear ends Lincoln’s nine-month unbeaten run Millwall start with 2-0 win over 10-man Bristol City Will Lankshear scored a second-half double on his debut as Middlesbrough fought back to kick off their Championship campaign with a hard-fought 2-1 victory, ending promoted Lincoln’s remarkable nine-month unbeaten run. The Imps – playing their first second-tier match in 65 years – made a strong start and opened the scoring in the 12th minute through Adam Reach. But the former Tottenham forward Lankshear marked his first league appearance since his move to the Riverside by equalising just after the hour and then stabbing in a stoppage-time winner. items.title: Belgian Pocognoli frontrunner to be Scotland boss
items.summary: Former Monaco head coach Sebastien Pocognoli is identified by the Scottish FA as their prime candidate to replace Steve Clarke.

items.title: Scotland hope to name 39-year-old Pocognoli as successor to Clarke in fresh approach
items.summary: Belgian would be first non-Scot in role since Berti Vogts Scotland face Slovenia on 26 September in Nations League The Scottish Football Association hopes to name the Belgian Sébastien Pocognoli as the successor to Steve Clarke as manager early next week. The 39-year-old, who was sacked by Monaco in June, will become the country’s first non-Scottish manager since Berti Vogts, who was in charge from 2002-04. Clarke’s abrupt departure came as Scotland exited the World Cup at the group stage. He had signed a four-year contract extension immediately before the tournament. It quickly became clear the SFA would turn towards a foreign manager; Jon Dahl Tomasson and Kasper Hjulmand were linked with the position. Continue reading...

items.title: Women’s U20 World Cup boycott may hurt in short term but can send Fifa a vital message | Tom Garry
items.summary: Women’s football has much to gain from the kind of reforms that threats to snub upcoming tournaments might prompt. Infantino should be taken on “And I say to all the women … Pick the right battles. Pick the right fights. You have the power to change. You have the power to convince us men what we have to do and what we don’t have to do. You do it. Just do it. With men, with Fifa, you will find open doors. Just push the doors. They are open.” Those were the condescending words of Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, three years ago during a tone-deaf speech in Sydney, which left his audience, including some of the most senior women in the game, exasperated. It is a damning indictment of Infantino’s tenure that his patronising monologue on the eve of the Women’s World Cup final now barely even creeps into the top 10 of the most controversial moments since his latest re-election, in March 2023. Continue reading...

items.title: London City Lionesses’ Mapi León: ‘It is a club created for women. It is beautiful and exciting’
items.summary: Spain defender on swapping Barcelona for Bromley, embracing the contrasting style of the WSL – and her newfound love for beans and crumpets ‘No, I can’t, I’m sorry, it’s a secret!” Mapi León roars with laughter, in response to being asked what persuaded her to join London City Lionesses. Does this bode badly for our interview? Fear not, the Spain centre-back is in as banterous and jovial a mood as you could imagine any new signing to be, as she embarks on her first major interview since signing for the Women’s Super League club. Across the course of our conversation, in bright sunshine outside a quiet hotel near Maidstone, it is evident that the 31-year-old could scarcely be happier about her decision to swap Barcelona for south-east England. She is sorely missing her cat, Bagheera (“Here, you ask for so many things for pets, you can’t [really] fly with them, it’s so many documents, so many things”) but, that aside, she is buoyant, relaxed and clearly embracing English life. She says she likes the “little bread” in the morning, and we eventually establish she is referring to crumpets, and reveals: “I like the beans in the morning. It’s really interesting. My Spanish teammates like Alexia [Putellas] and Jana [Fernández] are like: ‘What are you doing eating beans in the morning? You need to train.’ I go: ‘No, it’s fine I like it.’” Continue reading...
